design: DESIGN-8 (owner-approved direction 2026-10-29): build 447 steps 1-4 for single-node requests; build 448 step 5 (REVAS: the family verifier on every unadmitted local start, repair-mode escalation, DESIGN-6 O5) and ledger p_fail learning; round 3 of the 448 review: one population, the runtime's escalation event priced for every row, repair within the family, no class certificate in the law path, small talk in every lane and turn, a small-talk local prompt
objective: same result as the newest top model at its highest reasoning, with less quota

pool_units.anthropic_shared: Cw: % of the Claude weekly pool (all models)
pool_units.openai_codex: Px: % of one Codex Pro weekly pool

cost_shape_source: a route is priced before it runs: the answer shape is every turn of two calls or fewer, whatever its realized output (review of 447); a workspace writer whose reading does work (a design, write or action task, or a workspace or execution need) is priced agentic (Core)

exchange.formula: price(pool) = ttr_w / remaining_w for w = the pool's unit window (its longest open window, the weekly one: Q is in its units); remaining_w = 1 - used_w/100; ttr_w = (resets_at_w - now) / window_length_w; any other window exhausted: no price (the pool cannot be drawn)
exchange.source: lead correction 2 (DESIGN-8, 2026-10-29): each pool priced by the share of its remaining allowance until its reset, from the providers' rate-limit data (routing_law.pools, the host's observations); no 1:1 and no headroom-threshold constant
exchange.stale_fallback: stale (past the host's valid_until_ms): each window not yet reset at its last observed share left with the whole window ahead (1 / remaining_w; plan usage only rises inside a window), an exhausted one no price until its reset (review of 447: a failed probe never prices a pool last seen scarce at pace); every window reset since, or no observation: the pool's smallest dispatchable remaining share with the whole window ahead (1 / remaining); no share at all: 1 (pace)

p_fail_inheritance: Round 3 of the 448 review (lead decision 2): E[Q] prices the event on which the RUNTIME escalates, and that escalation's step, for every row, and the release gate is judged on that draw (law_model is a report only). A pool reference is the top of the frontier and nothing runs after it: Q alone. A writer below the reference binds no ladder, so nothing runs after it either: Q alone (the step the law would take, its pool reference's answer, is the law_model report). A read-only row below the reference admitted with evidence (form b or c; an audited local row) escalates only on the runtime's STRUCTURAL screen failure (descentStructurallySound: empty, cut off, an error; a tier gap never triggers it and is never priced), to the full answer at its target: Q + p_screen x Q(target). p_screen (Core lawScreenPFail) is measured from the ledger's screened attempts, the same screen for every row, keyed model@effort and pooled over families and surfaces, Laplace-smoothed: a row with evidence starts from its own pool reference's screen rate and its own screened attempts move it at the prior's weight, (f_c + runs_prior * p_ref) / (n_c + runs_prior); the references learn p_ref from a SHADOW structural screen recorded on every law-bound reference answer (never gating it; before round 3 no reference was ever screened and every row inherited the bare prior forever). A row admitted by a deterministic verifier (form a) is priced per class of its failures (Core lawDetClassPFail): p(repair) x Q_det_repair(T) + p(full) x Q_answer(T) at the family's reference T, the class rates from the verifier's judged outcomes on the same held-out request population (decision 1). A local REVAS verified start keeps its own Laplace estimate from its REVAS checks.
p_fail_learning: build 448 (DESIGN-8 step 5: every outcome updates p_fail): the committed ledger snapshot (judged runs and structural screens up to its through_ms) is the table's p_fail and p_screen; Core adds its own routing ledger's records settled after through_ms, by the same two counting rules (Core lawJudgedOutcome, keyed model@effort|law family from each record's law receipt; Core lawScreenOutcome, keyed model@effort). A judged outcome is the verdict of the verifier the law applies to that row: for the local model its REVAS check (revas_pass, revas_fail), its family's deterministic verifier (det_pass, det_fail, with the failure's class: full when no deliverable draft, else repair) or a structural failure (empty, not returned); for any other row its verifier or check verdict or structural screen. A REVAS check or repair attempt (a deterministic verifier's repair included) and an escalated attempt are never descents; a small-talk request's outcome is never recorded under another family (round 3: no re-read).

value_of_information.pass_rule: an answer passes when the local model grades every item of its frozen checklist as met; a question is informative when the audit reference's answer passes; FAIL when any question has the reference passing and the cell failing (a discordant pair); PASS when there is none and at least n questions are informative; else INCONCLUSIVE (never admits; more questions are planned). A PASS admits (form c) only as a parity audit: n = n_parity informative questions sampled at random across the family (review of 447); a cost-sized pass is provisional and admits nothing
value_of_information.source: DESIGN-8 step 6 moved into 447 (lead correction 3): horizon 7 days and the cap <= 1% of a pool's weekly allowance per week are DESIGN-8's; n is the parity bound ceil(ln(1 - confidence) / ln(1 - s * tau)) (review of 447: tau the family tiers' tightest percentage tau, s the grader's measured sensitivity); the confidence 0.9 is declared here and is NOT derived: it awaits the lead's decision (review of 447)

effort_label_source: O4 (owner 2026-10-29): the Claude app labels Max '3.5x or more usage'; applied against the next-lower step and only ever raising cost

local_start.rule: DESIGN-8 step 2 (build 448): the local model is ADMISSIBLE for a family only by (a) a deterministic family verifier (deterministic_verifiers below: small talk F1) or (c) a passed parity paired audit of local@none|family, like any other row. Until then it may only START as a REVAS verified start, and only when that start is the argmin at its full price: E[Q] = Q_verify(j) + p_fail(local, family) x Q_repair(j), j the admissible row (a pool reference, or matched-tier or audit evidence) minimizing it. Step 5 runs j's check on every such local answer: a pass adopts the draft; a fail is a repair-mode escalation at j (DESIGN-6 O5: the draft plus the findings, the request and draft prefix reused, fix only what failed). The owner's 447 local-first order is no admission basis (step 2 does not allow it).
local_start.verifier: the cheapest independent check the law can justify for a tool-free answer family: an admissible row's review of the draft against the request (REVAS: PASS, or FAIL with a numbered list of what is wrong or missing). A structural or self-consistency check by the local model itself costs nothing and is NOT independent evidence of the reference's result (the 447 screen passed q2's index error); the review has a measurable quota cost and is priced in E[Q] (the verify and repair cost shapes).
local_start.candidate_floor: capability only, never a family list: a tool-free answer family (tools none, shape answer), a reading with needs_tools none, a read-only node, the request alone (no named file or material), on its first turn, or on any turn for a family with a deterministic verifier (round 3, decision 5: the check reads the reply alone); the host offers the local row for light tool-free readings (Swift lawMayAnswerLocally)
local_start.draft_max_tokens_source: rcc-plugin.mjs LOCAL_WORKER_MAX_TOKENS: the local worker's completion cap, the deterministic upper bound of a draft
local_start.check_pricing: verify(j): j's answer anchor (the shape's measured OS-1 context) plus the draft (uncached) as input, j's answer output as output; repair(j) at the same row inside the provider cache window: the request and draft prefix cached, the findings (bounded by the verify output) uncached, j's answer output as output. Both are upper bounds while no check is measured (O4: the expensive reading when uncertain): a check never outputs more than answering and a repair never more than rewriting. Every check and repair attempt's usage is in the routing ledger for measurement.
local_start.source: lead order for build 448 (2026-10-30): live q2 on 447 ('파이썬 list와 tuple 차이 설명해봐', law F2) bound the local row on basis owner_order and delivered a factual error past the structural screen

deterministic_verifiers_rule: DESIGN-8 step 2 (a) (lead order for build 448, 2026-10-31; reviews of 448): a family whose reference result has no factual content has a quality criterion Core checks with its own code. Small talk (F1), no_claim_reply_v2: a CLOSED grammar (Core lawDeterministicCheck): every clause of the reply is built from closed small-talk lists and the nouns of the owner's own declarative words and ends in a closed courtesy head; empathy and congratulations only for what the request names; a first-person clause only with the reply's own courtesy feeling or its wish for the owner; the owner's language with no letter of another script; within the local worker's completion cap D (the local row only). It admits rows only for the law family it was made for and only after its pre-registered held-out validation passed: zero false passes on every frozen labeled set (the compiler refuses an id without it). It admits every row whose answer it reads (a read-only node's law attempt; round 3, decision 5: small talk's node runs read-only in any lane, and the local start binds on any turn, the check reading the reply alone), each charged its rates ON IT, per class (lawDetClassPFail): every row starts from the same prior, the verifier's measured rejections of reference-quality replies (the references' own verdicts once a snapshot or the ledger has them, else the clean replies of its held-out sets judged as a pool row's), and its own judged verdicts move it at the prior's weight, measured on the SAME requests (round 3, decision 1: the local model's drafts, production small-talk prompt, of the held-out sets' own requests; the corpus drafts that price the realized gate never enter the fit). Round 3 (decision 3): any failure escalates WITHIN the family, once, to the family's reference fixed at bind (the runnable pool reference minimizing the priced step): repair mode (DESIGN-6 O5) with the draft plus the verifier's findings (lawDeterministicFindings), or the full answer when there is no draft; 448's F1 -> F2 re-read is removed. With no runnable reference (every pool exhausted) a pass is evidence by itself and the row stays admissible: a failure holds the request with the draft withheld (round 2, B). A family whose result has factual content (F2 and every other) has none.

conditions_source: tiers.json's conditional tiers (review of 447: none is dropped). A condition the reading can express is its predicate: 'the file is code' / 'a large code file or a repository' = domain coding; 'solve graduate-level science problems' = a science reading that is not an explanation; 'multi-step agentic work on a repository' / 'deep / multi-step build' = the node writes, executes or is read deep; 'graduate-level technical depth' = deep. A condition no reading can tell ('asserts specific facts', 'medical', 'charts/figures', 'an open/novel problem', 'GUI operation') applies always: the floor. An unread request (no reading) meets every reading clause.
